correctness.rationale: On 1-perp the connected graph Laplacian is positive definite. The inverse trace is strictly convex under any nonzero symmetric Laplacian perturbation; injectivity of off-diagonal weights and cyclic averaging establish unrestricted uniqueness. Positivity of the objective under global edge scaling rules out holding; Fourier diagonalization gives the exact strictly convex scalar problem and a unique interior root (positive derivative at epsilon=1, nonoptimal other endpoint). A sine partial fraction plus Poisson-kernel roots-of-unity sum proves the exact finite-n resolvent. Comparison and lower-bound arguments trap epsilon*n^(2/3) away from zero and infinity, and a uniform two-term expansion proves 4^(2/3) and the correction constant. An independent finite-size matrix inverse matches the Fourier objective and 986 finite diagnostics passed; those checks are corroboration, not proof of the infinite result.

value.rationale: The exact optimum of a natural family of spatially local reversible Markov chains is characterized for all sizes, unrestricted edge allocations and holding, with a singular two-channel limit: the short-step probability is positive yet vanishes as n^(-2/3), unlike the n^(-2) fastest-spectral-mixing objective. The leading Kemeny sum improves fourfold over nearest-neighbor dynamics, and the sharp n^(4/3) second-order penalty exposes the mechanism. This is not a routine known-table evaluation or merely a generic convexity observation.
